---
title: "Sequence encoding of run histories"
subtitle: "Paper 5 in a series on UK All-Weather racing outcomes"
author: "Patrick Gillen"
date: "2026-09-08"
abstract: |
  Papers 1 to 3 gave a model of UK All-Weather Flat handicaps a horse's
  recent form as a handful of hand-built features: last time out's finishing
  position if it was in the first four, the position two runs back on the
  same rule, whether the horse had ever won, and a small going-affinity
  block. This paper changes how that history reaches the model. Those
  features are removed and a gated recurrent encoder reads the horse's
  twenty most recent prior runs directly, eight values a run, with the raw
  finishing position rather than a top-four code. Everything else is held
  fixed: the same races, the same depth-three Plackett–Luce likelihood, the
  same downstream scorer. On
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p5"); u <- targets::tar_read(p5_test_race_universe, store = S); format(u$n_races[u$source == "common"], big.mark = ",") })`
  held-out test races the encoder beats the hand-built features on every
  ranking measure, every interval excluding zero, and beats paper 3's
  gradient-boosted trees by more; Section 1 gives the figures. Three models
  now separate cleanly on a test split where papers 1 to 3 could not be told
  apart. Two further findings: a multi-layer perceptron on identical
  features beat a linear scorer, which paper 3's conclusion about function
  class did not anticipate; and learned entity representations for trainer,
  jockey and sire lost to the strike rates they replaced, both intervals
  excluding zero. The market still ranks better than any of these models.
  The single-bet win backtest improves to
  `r local({ S <- file.path(rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj")), "_targets_p5"); b <- targets::tar_read(p5_test_backtests, store = S); sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * b$roi[b$arm == "rung3b" & b$bet == "win"]) })`,
  the best in the series, but the difference from paper 3 cannot be
  distinguished from zero.
format:
  html: default
  pdf:
    toc: true
    number-sections: true
bibliography: references.bib
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(targets)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(glue)

# Paper 5 reads the paper-5 store, not the main one. Like paper 4 and unlike
# papers 1-3 this does NOT call tar_config_set(): that writes the
# project-root `_targets.yaml`, which papers 1-3's own setup chunks also
# write, and pointing it at `_targets_p5` would send their next render at
# the wrong store. Passing `store =` per call leaves `_targets.yaml`
# untouched.
P5_ROOT <- rprojroot::find_root(rprojroot::has_file("awracing.Rproj"))
P5_STORE <- file.path(P5_ROOT, "_targets_p5")

# Sourced robustly across the cwd tar_quarto() sets (project root) and the
# one a direct render would set (this folder).
source(file.path(P5_ROOT, "papers", "05_encoder", "_helpers.R"))

# tar_load() centrally so tarchetypes::tar_quarto() picks these up as render
# dependencies — files pulled in via {{< include >}} are not auto-scanned.
tar_load(c(
  # scope, slice, sequences (_02)
  p5_slice, p5_frame, p5_sequences, p5_sequence_summary,
  p5_sequence_identity, p5_beaten_audit, p5_runners_interactions,
  p5_qualifying_runners, p5_arm_data, p5_scorable,
  # method (_03)
  p5_control_terms, p5_rung3b_terms, p5_configs_v4_mlp, p5_configs_v7,
  p5_diag_linear, p5_backend,
  # the ladder on validation (_04)
  p5_budget_decomposition, p5_mlp_vs_linear_v4, p5_mlp_scores_v4,
  p5_linear_scores_v4, p5_mlp_selected_v4, p5_linear_selected_v4,
  p5_rung2_vs_rung1, p5_rung2_scores, p5_rung2_selected, p5_entity_indices,
  p5_rung3_vs_rung1, p5_rung3_selected, p5_rung3b_scores_60,
  p5_rung3b_vs_rung3, p5_rung3b_selected, p5_rung3b_budget_check,
  p5_rung3b_decomposition, p5_test_arm_choice,
  # the test split (_05)
  p5_test_race_universe, p5_test_contrasts,
  p5_test_backtests, p5_roi_contrasts, p5_roi_units_check,
  p5_test_fit_rung1, p5_test_fit_rung3b,
  p5_gbt_train_data, p5_gbt_test_data,
  # diagnostics (_06)
  p5_encoder_diag, p5_seq_length_table
), store = P5_STORE)

# ---- quantities used in more than one section -----------------------------

n_test_races  <- p5_test_race_universe$n_races[
  p5_test_race_universe$source == "common"]
n_val_races   <- p5_slice$n_races_val
n_fit_races   <- p5_slice$n_races_fit
n_train_races <- p5_test_fit_rung1$n_train_races
n_train_rows  <- p5_test_fit_rung1$n_train_rows
n_test_rows   <- nrow(p5_gbt_test_data$key)

loss_2b     <- p5_arm_loss(p5_rung3b_decomposition, "paper 2b")
loss_linear <- p5_arm_loss(p5_rung3b_decomposition, "linear in torch")
loss_rung1  <- p5_arm_loss(p5_rung3b_decomposition, "rung 1 MLP")
loss_rung2  <- p5_arm_loss(p5_rung3b_decomposition, "rung 2 MLP")
loss_rung3  <- p5_arm_loss(p5_rung3b_decomposition, "rung 3 GRU")
loss_rung3b <- p5_arm_loss(p5_rung3b_decomposition, "rung 3b GRU")

gain_encoder     <- loss_rung1 - loss_rung3b
gain_nonlinear   <- loss_linear - loss_rung1
gain_ninefeature <- loss_2b - loss_linear
cost_embeddings  <- loss_rung2 - loss_rung1

# The market baseline as papers 2b and 3 published it. Not recomputed here
# and not contrasted here; quoted for context only.
market_p1    <- 0.00543
market_brier <- 0.1875
```

# Acknowledgments {.unnumbered}

I have been interested in modelling horse racing since first acquiring the
Smartform database more than a decade ago. The project has been picked up
and put down many times, the obstacle almost always being the gap between
an idea and a running implementation. What is different now is that working
alongside Claude Code (Anthropic's coding agent), with web-based Claude as a
research companion, has compressed that gap dramatically. I am grateful to
my brother, Michael Gillen, for the suggestion to build the model on
All-Weather races — the foundation of the scope choices set out in
@sec-data. The design choices — dataset, scope, model, comparison,
editorial line — are mine. The implementation, the bulk of the draft prose,
and a great deal of the verification were Claude Code's, under my direction;
every output was reviewed and edited before it reached the paper.
